title: Separation of duties for AI work
subtitle: Independent gatekeepers, reviewers from a different vendor, and failures that stay failures

stats.label: gates audited in the eighth phase of the swarm build
failed gates kept as failures, not narrowed away
unrelated gate dropped by explicit decision

lede: AI reviewers have two failure modes. Left alone they re-litigate forever. Drawn from the same model as the builder they share its blind spots and pass its mistakes. I applied the principle regulated industries use: the people who build do not judge, the judges are independent, and a failure stays a failure until it is fixed. In my system the builders, the quality reviewers, the gatekeeper and the adversarial reviewer are separate agents, the reviewers run on a different vendor's models from the builders, and a phase with two failed gates is held at a conditional pass with two failures. Agent teams report success. They are built to complete tasks and they complete the task of saying so.
quote: Adding a role would have let builders stop testing.
evidence: Separation of duties for AI work: builders, quality reviewers, a gatekeeper and an adversarial reviewer as separate agents, with the reviewers on a different vendor's models from the builders.

Evidence-gated acceptance: a phase audited against 27 gates held at a conditional pass, its 2 failed gates kept as failures and 1 unrelated gate dropped by explicit decision rather than by narrowing the criteria.
Multi-agent governance: follow-up review scoped to the findings it was opened for so AI review converges, and a FAIL stays a FAIL until the fix is delivered and re-reviewed.

Quality engineering for AI-produced work: checksums scrubbed from reviewer packets so reviewers reasoned about delivered content, and testing kept a developer activity that produces evidence rather than a new role.
author: Corey James
